decisions.reason: The Definition introduces P2, couplings and the finite nonnegative square-root infimum; it does not assert the metric axioms. Its product-coupling proof establishes precisely well-definedness. thm-wasserstein-two-is-a-metric separately proves diagonal separation, symmetry and the gluing/Minkowski triangle inequality under AC. A descriptive title does not require duplicating that subsequent theorem.

The CC hypothesis and dependency were already present, so no missing axiom invalidates the flow theorem. However axiom_use and its contract mirror incorrectly restricted CC to scalar FTC despite step 5.1 invoking CC-dependent Lebesgue differentiation and a countable family of exceptional sets. Corrected both the declared use and the proof explanation: scalar FTC supplies one-sided averages; countably chosen null sets give a common good set. Contraction, variational estimates, inverse flow and compact-escape continuation remain valid.

The zero-indexed convention makes the unqualified 1/n and 1/j choices incomplete at zero. Both approximate-minimizer families are now explicitly indexed by positive integers, preserving the estimates and theorem. Tight marginal laws give tight couplings by the compact-product union bound; weak projections preserve marginals; bounded continuous cost truncations and monotone convergence prove attainment and lower semicontinuity.

F4 cited only sum, scalar-multiple and increasing-limit closure, so its claimed quotient closure was unsupported as a citation. Replaced that overstatement and proved the quotient measurability locally: since p>0, every component satisfies {j_i/p>r}={j_i-rp>0}, a Borel set by the actual cited closure rules. Kernel integration makes finite p and j Borel; Gaussian derivative bounds and a positive compact-tube minimum of p give integrable local velocity and Lipschitz bounds; weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives the action inequality and cutoff/Fubini testing gives the continuity equation.

On the original N-indexed product, two sequences differing only at coordinate zero have D=0, so D is not a metric and Prokhorov cannot be invoked as written. Replaced S by the explicitly positive-indexed product matching every finite gluing and embedding. Every coordinate is now detected, coordinatewise completeness and geometric-tail estimates give completeness, rational eventually-zero sequences give separability, and compact-coordinate products give tightness. Adjacent optimal couplings then yield an almost-sure summable-increment limit with L2 tail control and hence W2 convergence. Also completed the reverse topology inclusion and cited the metric theorem for the final triangle inequality.

The witness n^(-2) needs positive indices; the statement already used sup over n>=1 but did not explicitly assign that domain to its sequence. Specified (mu_n) indexed by positive integers in Statement and Given, so every witness weight is defined, nonnegative, and sums with its complement to one. Its second moment is one and every coupling to delta_0 has that forced cost. The main equivalence remains unchanged: vanishing optimal L2 displacement gives narrow convergence and uniform tails; the finite continuity-cell matching plus residual product coupling proves the converse.

The example omitted the ambient dimension declaration required by its Euclidean Wasserstein definition. Added an integer d>=1 to the Example and Given without changing the translation, speed, continuity equation or minimal-action claim. The sole Dirac-pair coupling gives W2=|t-s||b|, the smooth-test chain rule integrates to zero, and the existing minimum-velocity theorem applies under the retained AC assumption to give minimum action T|b|^2, including b=0.
